title: From Text to Vision to Voice Exploring Multimodality with Open AI: Romain Huet
talk_summary: This is an OpenAI developer-experience keynote demoing GPT-4o multimodality (voice, vision, screen-share coding help), Sora, and voice cloning, plus a roadmap of four priorities: textual intelligence, faster/cheaper models, customization, and agents.

takeaways.technique: Batch API for async workloads at ~50% discount
takeaways.what_they_do: Route non-latency-sensitive jobs (document/image analysis, bulk processing) through an asynchronous batch endpoint priced at roughly half of synchronous calls.
takeaways.evidence_quote: all that can be for another 50% uh discount on pricing

takeaways.technique: Tiered model sizes by task difficulty
takeaways.what_they_do: Explicitly acknowledge not every use case needs top intelligence and plan multiple model sizes/prices so builders can match model to task.
takeaways.evidence_quote: we know that not every use case requires like the highest intelligence

takeaways.what_they_do: Demo shows the model reading a rendered UI plus pasted component code to spot a responsive-layout defect and suggest a concrete Tailwind fix.
takeaways.evidence_quote: When you switch to the mobile view, the layout looks a bit cramped and the images seem squished.

takeaways.what_they_do: Speaker notes using one assistant to reason out loud and produce the prompt for a coding tool (Cursor), i.e., a planner model writing instructions for an executor.
takeaways.evidence_quote: what should I prompt cursor? And I've done that many times
